node.title: Re: Using lazy list with a for loop (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
... make use of an iterator or tied array and avoid accumulating, but I would also like to keep the current user interface of simply iteratoring over the results with a for loop. Is this possible?

You could use a [doc://tie]d array in a for loop if the number of items is known in advance (FETCHSIZE is called; see also my reply to the relatively recent thread [id://11147970]). Otherwise I recommend you bite the bullet and switch to while, as that's generally the way to work with iterators in Perl, and iterators are incredibly powerful, as [https://hop.perl.plover.com/|HOP] taught us. Such a while can often also be expressed as a C-style for(;;), but IMHO that doesn't always look as elegant as while and foreach.

Update: Another alternative is to provide a custom API for looping with a callback, for example like [mod://Mojo::Collection]'s ->each. I think it would be less performant than a while, though.
